Do a thorough DEEP-DIVE AUDIT of the Nxeon "Cold Email Engine" (a Next.js + Prisma + Postgres add-on at /opt/nxeon) and produce a flagship-grade overhaul plan. The owner feels it's "too barebones" and wants it to "feel like a real flagship cold email platform" (Instantly / Smartlead / Apollo / Lemlist class). READ-ONLY — do not modify code; produce a plan.

STUDY the current implementation completely:
- Prisma models in prisma/schema.prisma: Business, Contact, EmailList, EmailListMember, Brand, Suppression, ConsentRecord, ColdCampaign, SequenceStep, ColdSend, EmailEvent, SendingDomain, Inbox, WarmupState, DeliverabilityEvent, PlacementTest, MetricsDaily, HealthSnapshot + all coldemail enums.
- lib/coldemail/* (compliance.ts, sender.ts, warmup.ts, rotation.ts, analytics.ts, feedback.ts, dns.ts), worker/coldemail.ts, worker/coldemail-deliverability.ts.
- app/admin/coldemail/* (all pages: overview, businesses, lists, brands, campaigns, domains, warming, analytics, suppression, settings) + components/admin/coldemail/* + lib/actions-coldemail.ts.
- The research already done: /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/projects/coldemail/architecture.md and phase3-research.md.

Then RESEARCH (WebSearch) the actual current feature sets of flagship cold-email platforms in 2026 — Instantly, Smartlead, Apollo, Lemlist, Woodpecker, lemwarm, EmailBison — focusing on what makes them feel "flagship": e.g. unified master inbox / reply management, conversation threading, AI reply drafting, a visual sequence/step builder with conditions & A/B variants, spintax/personalization variables & custom fields, unlimited-inbox rotation dashboards, lead/CRM pipeline with statuses (interested/meeting-booked), unibox + team collaboration, deliverability suite (inbox placement, blacklist monitor, DNS/auth checker, bounce/complaint dashboards), email verification on import, sending schedules/timezones, campaign analytics with step-level + variant-level breakdowns, webhooks/API, sub-accounts/agency mode, template library, do-not-contact/CRM sync.

DELIVERABLE — write /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/projects/coldemail/overhaul-plan.md:
1. **Current state** — an honest inventory of exactly what's built vs. stubbed vs. missing, per subsystem (data, compliance, sending, warmup, analytics, UI/UX), with file references.
2. **Gap analysis vs flagship** — a table: capability | flagship has it | we have it (yes/partial/no) | impact.
3. **Overhaul plan** — a prioritized, phased build spec to reach flagship quality: the specific features + UX (unified inbox/reply management, visual sequence builder, CRM/lead pipeline, spintax/variables/custom fields, deliverability suite, email verification, sending schedules, richer analytics, templates, webhooks/API, agency sub-accounts), the schema additions each needs, and what's genuinely gated on external creds (a real sending domain, an ESP). Note which are pure UI/UX polish vs new subsystems.
4. **The single biggest thing** that would most make it feel flagship.

Return a ≤250-word summary: the top 5 gaps, and your recommended Phase-1-of-overhaul (the highest-impact slice to build first). Cite sources for the competitor features.

1	# Cold Email Engine — Architecture & Research
2	
3	**Status:** Research + planning only. No code, no DB writes, no external calls, no sending.
4	**Owner:** Nicholas / Nxeon. **Target deploy:** dev box `51.79.226.215`.
5	**Stack:** Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Prisma + Postgres. Standalone app **and** an add-on module inside the Nxeon admin portal.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Product Overview
10	
11	A **shared, multi-brand B2B outreach platform**. One engine, three sending brands:
12	
13	| Brand | Sells | Sending identity |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| **Nxeon** | VPS / hosting | nxeon-branded domain(s) |
16	| **Marketing Agency** | Websites | agency-branded domain(s) |
17	| **Ads Autopilot** | Ad management | ads-branded domain(s) |
18	
19	Each brand has its own verified sending domains, From identities, physical postal address, templates and signatures, but shares the same business/contact database, list-building, enrichment, sequence engine, tracking pipeline, and — critically — a **global suppression/compliance layer**.
20	
21	Core capabilities:
22	1. **Business records** — name, category, type, contact person, email, website, phone, location, size, etc.
23	2. **List-building** across many verticals (filters/segments over the business/contact store).
24	3. **Data enrichment** via licensed provider APIs.
25	4. **Campaign / sequence builder** — multi-step, conditional, per-brand.
26	5. **Sending infrastructure** — per-domain/day caps, warmup, rotation.
27	6. **Tracking** — open / click / reply / bounce / complaint.
28	7. **Unified compliance layer** — suppression, unsubscribe, consent basis, audit.
29	
30	---
31	
32	## 2. Competitive Landscape (2025–2026)
33	
34	| Tool | Positioning | Pricing (approx) | Deliverability (independent tests) | Notes |
35	|---|---|---|---|---|
36	| **Instantly** | High-volume sending, unlimited inboxes | ~$97/mo Hypergrowth (5 users) | ~78% inbox placement | Simplicity + scale; built-in warmup pool |
37	| **Smartlead** | Technical multi-mailbox control | ~$94/seat flat | ~85% (best) | SmartDelivery suite, spam-score monitoring |
38	| **Lemlist** | Personalization (dynamic images/video), multichannel | ~$69/seat/mo (raised Feb 2026) | ~62% (weakest) | Lemwarm; personalization over placement |
39	| **Apollo.io** | All-in-one: data + sending | ~$49/mo entry, ~$395/mo teams | — | 275M+ contacts bundled |
40	| **Reply.io** | Multichannel + unlimited warmup | per-seat | — | — |
41	
42	**Takeaway for us:** we win by (a) owning the data + engine in-house across three brands, (b) baking compliance in as a first-class differentiator, and (c) integrating with Nxeon's self-hosted mail. We don't need to beat Smartlead on raw placement day one; we need correctness and multi-brand isolation.
43	
44	Sources: Instantly/Smartlead/Lemlist comparison articles (instantly.ai, seraleads.com, devcommx.com, 2026).
45	
46	---
47	
48	## 3. Data Sourcing Options (providers, pricing, ToS)
49	
50	### 3.1 Licensed provider APIs (preferred, lower legal risk)
51	
52	| Provider | Data | Entry pricing | Cold-outreach ToS posture |
53	|---|---|---|---|
54	| **Apollo.io** | 275M+ contacts, all-in-one | from ~$49/mo | License is **internal business use only**; **no sublicensing/reselling/sharing** the API or data. Export to CSV/CRM allowed for own use. Provides a GDPR DPA. Nov 2025: email-permutation validation restricted to new users. |
55	| **Hunter.io** | Email finder/verifier | from ~$34/mo | Email discovery + verification; good as an enrichment/verification layer. |
56	| **People Data Labs** | 1.5B+ profiles, pure API infra | from ~$98/mo, ~$0.01/record | Best for building an enrichment pipeline; no GTM layer. Licensing is the vendor's compliance basis. |
57	| **Clearbit** (now HubSpot Breeze Intelligence) | Firmographic enrichment | HubSpot-native | Best if HubSpot-native; less standalone. |
58	| **RocketReach / Lusha / Snov / Tomba** | Contact discovery | ~$33/mo+ | Secondary sources / fallbacks. |
59	| **Google Places (New) API** | Local-business firmographics (name, category, phone, website, location) | Since Mar 2025 per-SKU free caps (Essentials 10k, Pro 5k, Enterprise 1k events); subscription tiers $100/$275/$1,200 | **ToS caching restriction is critical** — most Places content (incl. phone) may **not be stored/cached beyond 30 days**; only `place_id` is exempt. No exporting/scraping Maps content out of the service. Great for *discovering* local verticals, but you must **re-enrich, not warehouse**, and pull the actual email elsewhere (Places rarely returns email). |
60	
61	### 3.2 Scraping vs. licensed data — legal/ToS assessment
62	
63	- **Collection vs. use are distinct legal events.** In the US there is no general law against scraping *public* data (cf. hiQ v. LinkedIn), so collecting a publicly listed business email is usually lawful **unless** the site's ToS forbids automated extraction — then it's a contract/ToS violation and potentially CFAA-adjacent risk.
64	- **The exposure is mostly on the *use* side:** sending to scraped addresses still must satisfy CAN-SPAM (US), GDPR + ePrivacy (EU), CASL (Canada).
65	- **Google Maps/Places specifically forbids** exporting/scraping Maps content and long-term caching — scraping Google's results is a direct ToS breach. Use the licensed API within its caching rules instead.
66	- **Recommendation:** default to **licensed providers** (compliance is partly the vendor's obligation, data is refreshable, DPAs exist). Treat any first-party scraping as opt-in, per-source ToS-reviewed, US-only-by-default, and always run it through the same suppression + verification + compliance gate. **Do not warehouse Google Places content beyond 30 days.**
67	
68	Sources: seamless.ai, mailerfind, skrapp, coldlytics (scraping legality); Apollo ToS (apollo.io/terms, apollo.io/terms/api); Google Places usage/billing + policies (developers.google.com); Lusha/Explorium/Autobound provider comparisons (2026).
69	
70	---
71	
72	## 4. Sending Infrastructure & Deliverability
73	
74	### 4.1 ESP / relay options
75	
76	| Option | Cost | Cold-email fit |
77	|---|---|---|
78	| **Amazon SES** | ~$0.10 / 1,000; dedicated IP ~$24.95/mo w/ full warmup control | Cheapest, permissive (transactional + marketing + cold), but you own reputation/warmup and AWS setup. **Primary candidate for scale.** |
79	| **Postmark** | $15/mo/10k; dedicated IP $50/mo | **Rejects cold email** — requires prior opt-in, transactional-focused. Not usable for cold outreach. Fine for our own system/transactional mail. |
80	| **SendGrid** | ~$19.95/mo Essentials; Pro $89.95 incl. dedicated IP | Flexible (transactional + marketing); shared-pool deliverability variable. Free tier gone (2025). |
81	| **Nxeon Mail (self-hosted, Mailcow)** | our infra | Full control of domains/IPs; per-memory, DKIM keys come from the **Mailcow API** (not the local resolver). Strong strategic fit for owning sending identity per brand. |
82	| **Instantly/Smartlead-style mailbox pools** | per-seat | Managed inbox rotation + warmup; we can emulate this ourselves. |
83	
84	**Plan:** abstract a `MailTransport` interface. Phase 1 uses **Amazon SES** (dedicated IPs per brand) and/or **Nxeon Mail (Mailcow)** for brand-owned domains. Postmark reserved for our own transactional/system email only. Never route cold outreach through Postmark.
85	
86	### 4.2 Authentication & deliverability (hard requirements)
87	
88	- **SPF + DKIM + DMARC on every sending domain.** Gmail/Yahoo (Feb–Jun 2024) *require* SPF+DKIM+DMARC for bulk senders (>5,000/day to Gmail); failing auth = reject/spam.
89	- **DKIM for Nxeon-Mail domains via Mailcow API** (per memory — the local resolver is not authoritative; I deleted the real DKIM record once already).
90	- **Domain/mailbox warmup:** start 5–15/day per inbox, ramp over 3–6 weeks to a **safe ceiling of 30–50/inbox/day** (the cap *includes* warmup traffic).
91	- **Sending caps** enforced per-domain and per-mailbox/day in the engine; rotation across mailboxes; throttled, jittered scheduling.
92	- **List hygiene:** keep bounce rate < 2%, Gmail Postmaster spam complaint rate well under **0.3%** (mitigations vanish above it). Verify every address (Hunter/PDL) before first send.
93	- **One-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058):** `List-Unsubscribe` + `List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` headers, HTTPS endpoint, honored within **48 hours** (Gmail/Yahoo requirement) — we'll honor immediately.
94	- Separate warmup pool traffic from live campaign traffic in scheduling math.
95	
96	Sources: Courier/EmailSendX/xmit ESP comparisons; Postmark support (broadcast/consent policy); instantly.ai, prospeo.io, smartlead.ai, unifygtm deliverability guides; RFC 8058 (Valimail, Mailgun, Postmark, EmailLabs).
97	
98	---
99	
100	## 5. Compliance Layer (FIRST-CLASS — the core of the design)
101	
102	### 5.1 What is legally required for B2B cold email
103	
104	**US — CAN-SPAM** (no B2B exemption; applies to cold B2B identically):
105	- Accurate **From/To/Reply-To/routing headers** — no false or misleading header info.
106	- **Non-deceptive subject lines.**
107	- **Valid physical postal address** in every message.
108	- **Functional opt-out**, honored within **10 business days**.
109	- Monitor third parties acting on your behalf.
110	- Penalty: up to **$53,088 per violating email** (2025); FTC's $2.95M Verkada action (Aug 2024) is the largest to date.
111	- Opt-out model (no prior consent needed) — but every other rule still binds.
112	
113	**EU — GDPR + ePrivacy Directive** (ePrivacy often takes precedence for the *sending act*):
114	- Lawful basis for B2B cold email is usually **legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f))** — requires a documented **Legitimate Interest Assessment (LIA)**: Purpose, Necessity, Balancing.
115	- Message must be **relevant to the recipient's professional role**, identify the sender, and provide a working opt-out.
116	- **Country variance is real and must be modeled:** Germany (UWG) generally requires **prior consent** even B2B; France (CNIL) allows legitimate interest for B2B *but* demands strict opt-out; UK/many states allow the corporate-address B2B exemption.
117	- Data-subject rights (access, erasure), retention limits, DPA with processors.
118	- Enforcement active: fines €500 → €900,000+ (SOLOCAL, CNIL 2025).
119	
120	**Canada — CASL** (strictest; consent-based):
121	- Requires **express or implied consent**. Implied consent via **existing business relationship** (purchase/contract within 24 months; inquiry within 6 months) **or** a **conspicuously published** business email with **no statement against** unsolicited commercial email (CEM), and message relevant to their role.

127	### 5.2 How the architecture bakes it in
128	
129	1. **Global suppression list** (cross-brand + optional per-brand): every unsubscribe, bounce (hard), complaint, manual add, and provider-DNC is written here. **Every send is checked against suppression at queue-time AND at send-time.** Suppression is append-only and audited.

135	7. **Sending caps + warmup** enforced in the scheduler (per domain/mailbox/day).
136	8. **Bounce & complaint handling** — SES/Mailcow feedback + FBL → auto-suppress; complaint-rate circuit breaker pauses a domain/campaign above threshold.
137	9. **Retention & audit** — consent records ≥3 years (CASL); full event/audit log; data-subject erasure workflow (GDPR) that tombstones a contact while preserving a hashed suppression entry.
138	10. **Opt-out SLA timers** — surfaced in admin; honored in real time (well within 48h / 10 business days).

48	## 2) Email warming — current mechanics (2026)
49	
50	**Why it still exists:** Gmail and Microsoft tightened filtering; brand-new domains/inboxes are flagged immediately. Warmup builds a history of "normal, trusted" sending — gradually rising volume + positive engagement (opens, replies, marking important, rescuing from spam) — so that by the time a real campaign sends, the provider already trusts the sender. ([omnisend warmup 2026](https://www.omnisend.com/blog/warm-up-email-domain/), [reply.io warm-up 2026](https://reply.io/warm-up-email/))
51	
52	**Modern ramp schedule (consensus 2026):**
53	- New inbox starts ~**5–10 emails/day**, ramps to **40–50/day** over **2–4 weeks** (MailReach's default is ~10/day wk1 → 40–50 by wk4). A "fully warmed" inbox tops out around **50–100/day** at **3–5 weeks**. ([mailreach gmail warmup](https://www.mailreach.co/blog/gmail-warmup), [leadhaste timeline](https://leadhaste.com/blog/email-warmup-timeline-and-schedule))
54	- Pre-warmed inboxes can start higher (Smartlead guidance: ~80/day wk1 → 150–180 by day 30). ([litemail smartlead warmup](https://litemail.ai/blog/email-warmup-smartlead-best-tool-2026))
55	- **AI/adaptive ramp** is now standard: Smartlead/MailReach adjust ramp speed in real time off a live "health score" instead of a fixed daily increment. MailReach cites a network of 30,000+ Google Workspace / M365 accounts + a "Co-Pilot" that reads deliverability signals. ([maildeck warmup tools 2026](https://maildeck.co/blog/best-email-warm-up-tools-2026/))
56	
57	**Warmup activities the networks simulate:** send between pool inboxes, auto-open, auto-reply, mark-as-important/star, and **rescue from spam → move to inbox** (the strongest signal). Seed inboxes across Gmail/M365/Yahoo. ([smartlead warm-up guide](https://www.smartlead.ai/blog/email-warm-up-guide))
58	
59	**The 2026 debate — does artificial warmup still help, or now hurt?** This is genuinely contested and Phase 3 must be honest about it:
60	- **Against:** most warmup tools generate *artificial* opens/clicks between simulated inboxes — literally trying to manipulate the spam filters whose job is to protect real users. Recent Gmail/Yahoo updates that reward *long-term domain reputation and real authentication* are increasingly good at detecting these synthetic patterns, and **when detected can actively damage deliverability**. ([omnisend 2026](https://www.omnisend.com/blog/warm-up-email-domain/), [prospeo deliverability](https://prospeo.io/s/email-deliverability-best-practices))
61	- **For (quality networks):** Instantly's 2026 Cold Email Benchmark Report claims *private, vetted* networks deliver 20–30% higher post-warmup inbox placement than public pools, because they exclude spam traps and reputation-damaged domains before entry. ([leadhaste high-volume warmup](https://leadhaste.com/blog/email-warmup-for-high-volume-sending))
62	- **Emerging best practice:** favor **real engagement** — genuine replies from a small seed audience, low-and-slow real sends to engaged recipients, and steady authenticated volume — over synthetic pool traffic. The safest posture is warmup that produces *replies and spam-recovery on a vetted pool*, not mass auto-opens.

66	## 3) Deliverability tactics 2026
67	
68	**Isolate the sending domain (universal in 2026).** Never cold-send from the primary brand domain — at volume it now *burns* the primary. Buy separate lookalike domains (e.g. `try-brand.com`, `getbrand.co`) and send from a **subdomain** (`mail.` / `outreach.`) so any reputation damage is quarantined off the root. ([growleads subdomain](https://growleads.io/blog/subdomain-for-cold-email-protect-main-domain/), [unifygtm cold email 2026](https://www.unifygtm.com/explore/cold-email-2026-domain-setup-deliverability-sequences))
69	
70	**Domain + inbox rotation (the core scaling primitive):**
71	- Serious teams run **3–5 domains**, each with **4–6 inboxes**, rotating daily. ([firstsales domain rotation](https://firstsales.io/blog/email-domain-rotation/), [litemail inbox rotation](https://litemail.ai/blog/cold-email-agency-inbox-rotation-best-practices-2026))
72	- **Per-inbox daily cap: 20–40** for a warmed inbox (newer inboxes 10–15), i.e. **~100–250/domain/day** across 3–5 inboxes. Space sends **90–120s apart** across a sending window — 40 rapid sends in an hour reads as bot behavior. ([ozigi caps](https://ozigi.app/blog/how-many-cold-emails-per-day-without-spam))
73	
74	**Authentication (mandatory — see §5):** SPF + DKIM + DMARC on every sending domain, warmed 2–4 weeks before volume.
75	
76	**Custom tracking domain:** always use your own tracking subdomain (e.g. `t.mail-brand.com`) instead of the tool's shared one; shared tracking domains are widely blocklisted and tank placement. Only enable open tracking behind a custom domain (and see §4 on why opens barely matter now). ([mailflowauthority infra](https://mailflowauthority.com/cold-email/cold-email-infrastructure-complete-guide))
77	
78	**Content variation / spintax:** the #1 content-level deliverability killer is **duplicate content** — identical bodies to many recipients from one domain get fingerprinted as bulk. Spintax (`{Hi|Hello|Hey}`) makes each send unique. **Nuance:** word-level spintax "barely moves deliverability"; **sentence/paragraph-level variation with 6–10 meaningful variants** is where the lift is. Personalization matters more: emails with ≥2 personalizations get 5.6% reply vs 3.6% with none (Hunter.io 2026 State of Cold Email). ([smartlead spintax](https://www.smartlead.ai/blog/what-is-spintax), [mailreach spintax](https://www.mailreach.co/blog/spintax-cold-email))
79	
80	**Inbox-placement / seed testing:** don't trust "delivered" — test where mail actually lands.
81	- **GlockApps** — ~$59/mo, 70+ seed addresses (Gmail/Outlook/Yahoo/corporate + regional EU/APAC), reports inbox vs spam vs Promotions/Updates vs missing, plus DMARC analytics + blocklist monitoring + content analysis. ([mailflowauthority glockapps](https://mailflowauthority.com/esp-reviews/glockapps-review))
82	- **MailReach spam test** — 30+ real Google Workspace/M365/Gmail/Outlook/Yahoo mailboxes; inbox/spam/promotions breakdown. ([mailreach spam test tools](https://www.mailreach.co/blog/email-spam-test-tools))
83	
84	**List verification (pre-send, non-negotiable for bounce control):** ZeroBounce / NeverBounce / Bouncer / MillionVerifier all sit at **97–99% accuracy**. The real differentiator is **catch-all handling** (15–28% of B2B domains are catch-all where *no* tool can confirm the mailbox); Bouncer claims ~87% catch-all detection vs 40–60% for others. Verify every list immediately before send, not at import (addresses decay). ([instantly verification benchmark 2026](https://instantly.ai/blog/2026-email-verification-benchmark-accuracy-scores-for-8-top-tools/), [usebouncer best tools](https://www.usebouncer.com/best-email-verification-tools/))

86	**Bounce & complaint handling:** hard bounce → suppress permanently, never retry; soft bounce → limited retry then suppress; complaint (FBL/List-Unsubscribe) → suppress + investigate targeting (see §4 thresholds).

92	## 4) Analytics that actually matter now
93	
94	**Metric definitions (2026):**
95	- **Delivery rate** = accepted by receiving server ÷ sent. High delivery ≠ inbox; it only means "not bounced/rejected." Do not confuse with placement.
96	- **Inbox-placement rate** = of delivered mail, % landing in the primary inbox (vs spam/Promotions/missing). Measured via seed tests (§3), *not* from your own send logs. **Good ≥90%, best-in-class ≥95%.** ([amplemarket 2026 benchmarks](https://www.amplemarket.com/blog/cold-email-benchmarks))
97	- **Open rate** = pixel loads ÷ delivered. **Largely broken — see below.**
98	- **Click rate** = unique clickers ÷ delivered. More reliable than opens but distorted by security scanners/link-preview bots that auto-click.
99	- **Bounce rate** = bounces ÷ sent. **Hard bounce** = permanent (bad/nonexistent address) → suppress forever. **Soft bounce** = temporary (mailbox full, greylisting, size).
100	- **Spam-complaint rate** = complaints ÷ delivered (via Postmaster/FBL).
101	- **Unsubscribe rate** = unsubs ÷ delivered.
102	- **Reply rate** and **positive-reply rate** = replies (and positive/interested replies) ÷ delivered. **The KPI that matters most in 2026.**
103	
104	**Open tracking is unreliable — be honest in the UI.** Apple Mail Privacy Protection (since 2021, escalated through iOS 18) **pre-loads all remote content including tracking pixels on Apple's servers**, so emails register as "opened" even when unread. Apple Mail is ~51% of the global email-client market and **>55% of all global opens now come from Apple/MPP devices** — meaning the majority of "opens" are machine-generated. Corporate security scanners (Proofpoint/Mimecast/Defender) also pre-fetch pixels *and* links. **Net: open rate is inflated, non-comparable, and unsafe as an optimization target or a health signal.** ([sender.net MPP 2026 guide](https://www.sender.net/blog/apple-mail-privacy-protection/), [hustlermarketing 3 metrics replacing open rate](https://www.hustlermarketing.com/blog/3-email-metrics-that-are-replacing-open-rate-in-2026/), [instantly open-tracking accuracy](https://instantly.ai/blog/email-open-tracking-how-it-works-accuracy-rates-and-why-your-open-metrics-may-be-wrong/))
105	
106	**What leaders optimize instead (MPP-proof signals):**
107	1. **Reply rate / positive-reply rate** — replies require human intent; mailbox providers treat replies as a strong positive trust signal. This is the primary campaign KPI.
108	2. **Click rate** — MPP-resistant (MPP proxies pixels, not user clicks), though filter clicking distorts it.
109	3. **Complaint rate + bounce rate + unsubscribe rate** — combined into a "disaffection/disengagement" index; the clearest early warning of a burning domain.
110	4. **Inbox-placement rate** from seed tests — the ground truth for "are we even in the inbox."
111	
112	**Benchmarks (2026, deliverability-managed vs raw):**
113	| Metric | Good | Best-in-class | Danger |
114	|---|---|---|---|
115	| Inbox placement | ≥90% | ≥95% | <80% |
116	| Bounce | <3% | <1.5% | >5% → stop & diagnose |
117	| Reply | 1–5% | 8–10%+ | — |
118	| Spam complaint | <0.1% | ~0% | 0.3% hard ceiling |
119	| Open (context only) | 15–25% raw | not a target | ignore |
120	Source: [amplemarket 2026](https://www.amplemarket.com/blog/cold-email-benchmarks).
121	
122	**"Domain/inbox is burning" thresholds (auto-pause triggers):**
123	- **Bounce:** <2% safe · 2–5% warning (Postmaster reputation degrading, clean list before continuing) · >5% danger (immediate pause + re-verify). Sustained >2% for 5–7 days suppresses inbox placement for *all* Gmail recipients on that domain, not just the bad addresses. **Recommended auto-pause at ~1.8% per inbox/day** (before the ceiling). ([litemail bounce thresholds](https://litemail.ai/blog/cold-email-inbox-bounce-rate-thresholds-2026))
124	- **Complaint:** <0.05% safe · 0.05–0.08% warning · **>0.08% pause the whole domain and investigate targeting** (Google effectively treats ~0.1%+ as a problem; 0.3% is the hard mandate ceiling). Complaint spikes = wrong ICP or deceptive copy. ([amplemarket](https://www.amplemarket.com/blog/cold-email-benchmarks), [litemail health metrics](https://litemail.ai/blog/cold-email-inbox-health-metrics-2026))
125	
126	---
127	
128	## 5) CURRENT regulation + ISP requirements (the fast-changing part) — what's mandatory NOW
129	
130	This is what gates the inbox *at all* in 2026. Non-compliant senders see **22–34% of mail routed to spam vs 89% inbox placement for compliant senders** — a 3–7x penalty. ([mailover 2026 guide](https://mailover.ai/blog/bulk-sender-requirements.html))
131	
132	**Google + Yahoo — "Yahoogle" (announced Oct 2023, enforced Feb 1 2024), for senders of 5,000+/day to consumer Gmail/Yahoo:**
133	- **SPF + DKIM** both configured and passing; **at least one aligned** to the From-header domain.
134	- **DMARC** published, minimum **p=none** with a RUA reporting tag.
135	- **One-click unsubscribe** per **RFC 8058** (`List-Unsubscribe` + `List-Unsubscribe-Post`), processed **within 2 days**.
136	- **Spam complaint rate < 0.3%** (hard ceiling) via **Google Postmaster Tools**; operational target **< 0.1%**.
137	- Valid forward + reverse DNS (FCrDNS) and TLS on transmission.
138	- **Escalation:** Feb 2024 = temp deferrals (421-4.7.26/.30/.32); **Nov 2025 Gmail escalated to permanent rejection (550-5.7.26)** for unauthenticated mail. Full enforcement across providers in 2026. ([redsift 2026 checklist](https://redsift.com/guides/bulk-email-sender-requirements), [mailgun yahoogle](https://www.mailgun.com/state-of-email-deliverability/chapter/yahoogle-bulk-senders/), [autospf two years on](https://autospf.com/blog/google-yahoo-bulk-sender-mandate-changes-over-two-years/))
139	
140	**Microsoft / Outlook (enforced May 5 2025), for 5,000+/day to Outlook.com/Hotmail.com/Live.com:**
141	- **SPF + DKIM + DMARC** all required; DMARC min **p=none**, aligned to SPF or DKIM (ideally both).
142	- Non-compliant mail was first **junked**, moving toward **rejection**; treat SPF+DKIM+DMARC as mandatory to reach Outlook consumer inboxes. Microsoft doesn't publish the 0.3% number but the same hygiene applies. ([microsoft tech community](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoftdefenderforoffice365blog/strengthening-email-ecosystem-outlook%E2%80%99s-new-requirements-for-high%E2%80%90volume-senders/4399730), [mailgun MS requirements](https://www.mailgun.com/blog/deliverability/microsoft-sender-requirements/), [validity MS rules](https://www.validity.com/blog/keeping-the-inbox-safe-microsofts-new-bulk-email-rules-explained/))
143	
144	> **Cold-email caveat:** the 5,000/day thresholds are *per-provider consumer volume*. A rotation setup sending 20–40/inbox stays under it per inbox — but **compliance is not optional even below 5k**: sub-threshold senders that fail auth or spike complaints still get filtered, and the auth requirements are now the de-facto floor for *any* sender. Build to the strict standard regardless of volume.
145	
146	**Legislation (status + 2025–2026 changes):**
147	- **CAN-SPAM (US):** permissive — cold email allowed without prior consent, but requires accurate From/subject, a functional opt-out honored promptly, and a **valid physical postal address** (commonly missed). Penalty raised to **up to $53,088 per email, effective Jan 17 2025**. ([instantly compliance](https://instantly.ai/blog/b2b-email-list-compliance-gdpr-canspam/), [growleads is cold email legal 2026](https://growleads.io/blog/is-cold-email-legal-gdpr-can-spam-2026/))
148	- **GDPR (EU/UK):** B2B cold email allowed under **legitimate interest** (no explicit consent) *only* with a documented Legitimate Interest Assessment, business (not personal) addresses, role-relevant messaging, disclosure of data source, and easy opt-out. Fines up to **€20M / 4% global revenue**. **New:** France's **CNIL rules effective Aug 2026 require explicit opt-in for all B2C prospecting** (email/phone/SMS) — watch for other member states following. ([outreachbloom compliance 2026](https://outreachbloom.com/cold-email-compliance), [inboxkit compliance](https://www.inboxkit.com/learn/cold-email-compliance-gdpr-can-spam))
149	- **CASL (Canada):** strictest — **consent required before the first send** (express or implied via an existing business relationship in the last 2 years). Fines up to **$10M CAD/violation (orgs), $1M CAD (individuals)**. ([moderninbound compliance](https://moderninbound.com/blog/cold-email-compliance-guide))
150	- **2026 trend:** regulators are actively cracking down on unsolicited commercial email and **AI-generated outreach is accelerating enforcement / creating new exposure**. Suppression, consent records, and jurisdiction handling must be first-class, not bolted on.
151	
152	**Mandatory-NOW checklist to reach the inbox:** ① SPF + DKIM (aligned) on every sending domain · ② DMARC published (min p=none, RUA) · ③ RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe on marketing mail, honored ≤2 days · ④ complaint rate <0.3% (target <0.1%) monitored via Postmaster · ⑤ dedicated cold domain + subdomain, warmed · ⑥ verified list (bounce <3%) · ⑦ physical address + honest identification + working opt-out (CAN-SPAM) · ⑧ documented lawful basis per recipient jurisdiction (GDPR/CASL).
153	
154	---

156	# Cold Email Phase 3 — Build Spec
157	
158	Builds on the Phase 1/2 skeleton (businesses, contacts, lists, brands/sending-identities, suppression, one-click unsubscribe, gated send worker with warmup-ramp + daily caps, open/click tracking). Phase 3 = **warming, real analytics, and multi-domain/inbox rotation with health-based auto-pause**, plus baked-in compliance.
159	
160	## A. Data model additions (Prisma)
161	
162	**Domains & inboxes (the rotation substrate)**
163	- `SendingDomain` — `id, businessId, brandId, domain, subdomain, isPrimary(false), status(pending|warming|active|paused|burned), spfVerified, dkimVerified, dmarcPolicy(none|quarantine|reject), dmarcVerified, trackingDomain, trackingDomainVerified, addedAt, warmupStartedAt`.
164	- `Inbox` — `id, sendingDomainId, email, provider(gmail|m365|smtp|postal|kumo), imapConfig/smtpConfig(encrypted), status(warming|active|paused|burned), dailyCap, currentRampCap, warmupDay, lastSendAt, sendWindowStart/End, minGapSeconds(90–120), reputationScore(0–100)`.
165	- `InboxAuth` — SPF/DKIM/DMARC/tracking check results per domain with `lastCheckedAt` (re-verify on a schedule; DNS drifts).
166	
167	**Warmup schedule & state (per inbox)**
168	- `WarmupPlan` — `inboxId, strategy(conservative|standard|aggressive|adaptive), startCap, targetCap, rampDays, dailyIncrement, mode(pool|real-seed|hybrid)`.
169	- `WarmupState` — `inboxId, day, plannedToday, sentToday, warmupRepliesToday, spamRescuesToday, healthScore, pausedReason`.
170	- `WarmupActivity` — event log of pool interactions (sent/opened/replied/marked-important/rescued-from-spam) for auditability and the honesty argument (we can show *what kind* of warmup ran).
171	
172	**Deliverability events (the analytics spine)**
173	- `DeliverabilityEvent` — append-only: `id, inboxId, sendingDomainId, campaignId, contactId, messageId, type(sent|delivered|deferred|hard_bounce|soft_bounce|open|click|reply|positive_reply|complaint|unsubscribe|placement_test), subtype(bounce reason code, etc.), provider, occurredAt, raw`. Everything else rolls up from this table. Store SMTP/DSN codes so hard vs soft is derived, not guessed.
174	- `PlacementTest` — `id, sendingDomainId, provider(glockapps|mailreach|manual_seed), inbox%, spam%, promotions%, missing%, runAt` (seed-list results; the only trustworthy "in the inbox?" signal).
175	
176	**Analytics rollups (precomputed for dashboards)**

Roll up nightly + on-demand.
178	- `HealthSnapshot` — `(date, scope, scopeId, healthScore, status, triggeredRules[])` feeding auto-pause.
179	
180	**Compliance**
181	- `ConsentRecord` — `contactId, lawfulBasis(legitimate_interest|consent|existing_relationship), jurisdiction, source, assessmentRef, capturedAt`.
182	- Extend `Suppression` with `reason(hard_bounce|complaint|unsubscribe|manual|global)` and enforce **global cross-campaign** suppression (already present — keep it authoritative).
183	
184	## B. Warming UI
185	
186	- **Per-inbox warmup dashboard:** ramp curve (planned vs actual daily volume), current day / target, health score, and a plain-language status ("Warming — day 9 of 21, on track").
187	- **Strategy picker:** conservative / standard / adaptive, with mode = *pool* / *real-seed* / *hybrid*. **Default to hybrid/real-seed and surface a warning** that synthetic-pool warmup can be detected and may hurt in 2026 (cite the debate) — don't present artificial warmup as risk-free.
188	- **Warmup activity feed** (opens/replies/spam-rescues) so the customer sees it's working and *what kind* of signals ran.
189	- **"Ready to send" gate:** block campaign sends from an inbox until warmup day ≥ threshold AND auth (SPF/DKIM/DMARC/tracking) all green — reuse the existing gated send worker.
190	
191	## C. Analytics dashboards
192	
193	- **Campaign view:** delivery, bounce (hard/soft split), reply + **positive-reply** (hero metric), click, complaint, unsubscribe, inbox-placement. Time series + funnel.
194	- **Open rate: show it, but flag it.** Render behind an "⚠ inflated by Apple MPP / scanners — not a reliable signal" tooltip, visually de-emphasized, never the headline and never an optimization target. This honesty is a differentiator vs tools that still lead with opens.
195	- **Deliverability/health view (per inbox & per domain):** reputation score, rolling bounce%, complaint%, unsub%, latest placement-test result, and burn-risk status with the exact thresholds (§4). Color: green <2% bounce/<0.05% complaint, amber to 5%/0.08%, red beyond.
196	- **Placement testing:** trigger/seed-test integration (GlockApps/MailReach API or an internal seed list) and chart inbox-vs-spam-vs-promotions over time.
197	- **Roll-ups** at business level for the agency/multi-client case.
198	
199	## D. Multi-domain / multi-inbox management + rotation + auto-pause
200	
201	- **Pool manager:** register domains → subdomains → inboxes; run and cache SPF/DKIM/DMARC/tracking verification; show a readiness matrix.
202	- **Rotation engine** in the send worker: distribute a campaign's daily sends round-robin across *eligible* inboxes (status=active, under `currentRampCap`, warmup complete, auth green), spacing sends `minGapSeconds` (90–120s) inside each inbox's send window; respect per-inbox and per-domain caps (20–40/inbox, ~100–250/domain). Persist last-used to avoid clustering.
203	- **Auto-pause on bad metrics (the safety system):** evaluate `HealthSnapshot` rules continuously —
204	  - bounce ≥1.8%/inbox/day → **pause inbox**; sustained >2% over multiple days → **pause domain**; >5% → **hard stop + require re-verification**.
205	  - complaint >0.08%/domain → **pause domain + flag targeting**.
206	  - On pause: stop new sends, keep the inbox warming, notify, and require manual/verified re-activation. Never silently keep burning a domain.
207	- **Deliverability inbox rescue:** on soft-bounce spikes, back off volume automatically (adaptive ramp down), don't just hard-pause.

211	- **Auth-or-no-send:** worker refuses to send from any domain lacking passing SPF+DKIM+DMARC (min p=none). This is now table stakes (§5).
212	- **RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe** on every message (`List-Unsubscribe` + `List-Unsubscribe-Post`), processed automatically ≤2 days → global suppression. (Extend Phase 1/2's unsubscribe.)

215	- **Complaint-rate circuit breaker** wired to Postmaster/FBL data feeding the same auto-pause.
216	- **Global cross-campaign suppression** authoritative; never re-mail hard-bounces or complainers.
217	- **Verify-before-send:** integrate list verification (ZeroBounce/NeverBounce/Bouncer) as a pre-send step; block campaigns whose projected bounce (from verification) exceeds ~3%.

# Cold Email Engine — Flagship Overhaul Plan

**Compiled 2026-08-11 (READ-ONLY audit — no code changed).** Target: take the Nxeon Cold Email
add-on (`/opt/nxeon`, Next.js App Router + Prisma + Postgres) from a correct-but-barebones
*sender* to a flagship-class *outreach platform* (Instantly / Smartlead / Apollo / Lemlist tier).

The honest one-line verdict: **the compliance + deliverability engine is genuinely strong — arguably
better-architected than most competitors — but the product is send-only. It has no eyes and no
memory: it never reads a reply, never scores a lead, and gives the operator forms instead of a
workspace.** That is exactly why it feels barebones, and it is fixable without touching the good core.

---

## 1. Current state — honest inventory (what's built / stubbed / missing)

### Data model (`prisma/schema.prisma`) — **BUILT, solid**
Full Phase 1–3 schema exists and is well-commented: `Business`, `Contact` (+ `EmailStatus`),
`Brand` (sending identity), `EmailList`/`EmailListMember`, `Suppression` (GLOBAL/BRAND scope),
`ConsentRecord`, `ColdCampaign`, `SequenceStep`, `ColdSend`, `EmailEvent`, plus the deliverability
layer: `SendingDomain`, `Inbox`, `WarmupState`, `DeliverabilityEvent`, `PlacementTest`,
`MetricsDaily`, `HealthSnapshot`, and every enum. Additive, migration-safe.
- **Gaps in the model:** `SequenceStep` has only `subject/bodyMarkdown/delayDays` — **no condition,
  no A/B variant, no channel**. `Contact` has **no CRM stage/owner/status** and **no custom-field
  store**. `Inbox` declares `provider` (GMAIL/M365/SMTP/POSTAL/KUMO) but has **no SMTP/IMAP
  credential fields** — so "rotation" is really From-header rotation over one shared Mailcow relay,
  not per-mailbox sending. There is **no `Template`, no `Reply`/`Conversation`, no `ApiKey`/
  `Webhook`, no `Workspace`/tenant** model.

### Compliance (`lib/coldemail/compliance.ts`, `feedback.ts`) — **BUILT, flagship-grade**
Suppression matching (email+domain, global/brand tiers), stateless HMAC one-click unsubscribe (RFC
8058), open/click tokens, CAN-SPAM footer + postal-address enforcement, brand readiness checks,
**reputation isolation** (protected-domain set blocks cold-sending from `nxeon.cloud`), and a
complaint-rate **circuit breaker** that auto-pauses a brand (`feedback.ts`). This is a real
differentiator — keep it as the spine. **Stub:** `recordFeedback` is fed only by a manual action /
webhook *seam* (`app/api/coldemail/feedback/route.ts`) — no live SES-SNS or Mailcow FBL wired.

### Sending (`lib/coldemail/sender.ts`, `worker/coldemail.ts`) — **BUILT but single-relay + gated OFF**
Pure message rendering (markdown→HTML, `{{var}}` substitution, tracking injection), a `MailTransport`
interface with a working `NxeonSmtpTransport` and a **stub `SesTransport`**. The send worker is
correct and careful: idempotent scheduling, send-time suppression re-check, per-inbox warmup cap,
send-window, jittered throttle, rotation attribution. **Hard-gated behind `cold_email_sending_enabled`
(default false) — nothing sends today.** Limitation: all mail leaves via one platform SMTP config
(`loadSmtpConfig` reads global `Setting` rows); the inbox only changes the `From`.

### Warmup + rotation (`warmup.ts`, `rotation.ts`, `worker/coldemail-deliverability.ts`) — **BUILT (mechanics), synthetic engagement out of scope**
Pure ramp math (presets, adaptive health back-off, planned-vs-actual curve), rotation selection
(LRU + min-gap + cap), and health-based **auto-pause** (bounce/complaint thresholds straight from
research §4). A warmup sweep recomputes ramp caps and auto-promotes WARMING→ACTIVE. **Missing by
design:** there is no actual warmup *traffic* — no pool sends, no seed replies, no spam-rescue. The
`WarmupState.warmupReplies/spamRescues` columns are never populated. (Correct call — a real warmup
network can't be self-hosted — but the UI currently implies activity that doesn't happen.)

### Analytics (`lib/coldemail/analytics.ts`) — **BUILT, honest, but shallow presentation**
Excellent rate derivation and the **2026 open-rate honesty posture** (opens surfaced but flagged
MPP-unreliable, never a health input; reply/positive-reply are the hero KPIs) — a genuine
flagship-quality opinion competitors lack. Composite health score excludes opens. **Gaps:** rollups
are count tiles only — no time-series charts, **no step-level or variant-level breakdown**, and the
hero reply metrics **are always zero because nothing ingests replies** (see below).

### UI/UX (`app/admin/coldemail/*`, `components/admin/coldemail/*`) — **BARE — this is the felt problem**
Ten server-rendered pages (overview, businesses, lists, brands, campaigns, campaign detail, domains,
warming, analytics, suppression, settings). Everything is a **plain form + list**: sequence = an
`<ol>` of steps with an "Add a step" form (`campaigns/[id]/page.tsx`); domains/inboxes/seed-tests are
number-input forms (`Phase3Controls.tsx`). No drag-and-drop builder, no inbox/triage view, no
pipeline board, no charts, no template gallery. Functional, on-theme, but visibly a control panel,
not a product.

### The decisive missing subsystem: **REPLY INGESTION**
`EmailEventType.REPLY/POSITIVE_REPLY` exist and roll up, but **no code path writes them**. There is
**no IMAP poller, no reply parser, no conversation store, no inbox UI.** The platform is deaf: it can
send a sequence but cannot see that someone answered, cannot stop follow-ups on reply from the mail
side, cannot categorize interested vs not, cannot book a meeting. Every flagship competitor's
headline feature (unibox / master inbox) is precisely this, and it is 0% built.

---

## 2. Gap analysis vs flagship (2026)

Legend: **Yes** = comparable to flagship · **Partial** = present but thin/stubbed · **No** = absent.

| Capability | Flagship has it | We have it | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPF/DKIM/DMARC auth + verifier | ✅ | **Yes** (`dns.ts`, authoritative-NS verify) | — strong |
| One-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058) | ✅ | **Yes** | — strong |
| Suppression / DNC (global + scoped) | ✅ | **Yes** | — strong |
| Consent / lawful-basis records (GDPR/CASL) | Partial (most weak here) | **Yes** | **differentiator** |
| Reputation isolation + complaint circuit breaker | ✅ | **Yes** | **differentiator** |
| Warmup ramp + health auto-pause | ✅ | **Partial** (math yes; no real warmup traffic) | med |
| Domain/inbox rotation | ✅ | **Partial** (From-rotation over 1 relay; no per-mailbox creds) | **high** |
| Honest MPP-aware analytics | ✗ (most still lead w/ opens) | **Yes** | **differentiator** |
| **Unified master inbox / unibox** | ✅ (Instantly, Smartlead, Lemlist) | **No** | **critical** |
| **Reply capture (IMAP) + threading** | ✅ | **No** | **critical** |
| **AI reply categorization** (interested / meeting / OOO / not-interested…) | ✅ (Smartlead 9 buckets) | **No** | **high** |
| AI reply drafting | ✅ | **No** | med |
| **Visual sequence builder w/ conditions + branches** | ✅ (Smartlead subsequences, Woodpecker branches) | **No** (linear steps only) | **high** |
| **A/B variants per step, auto-winner** | ✅ (Woodpecker ≤5 variants) | **No** | **high** |
| **Spintax + rich personalization / custom fields** | ✅ (Lemlist liquid, dynamic images) | **Partial** (5 hardcoded `{{vars}}`) | **high** |
| **CRM / lead pipeline w/ statuses** | ✅ (Instantly & Smartlead built-in CRM) | **No** | **high** |
| **Pre-send email verification** | ✅ (Instantly, Woodpecker, Bouncer) | **No** (post-send bounce only) | **high** |
| **Deliverability suite** (placement test API, blacklist monitor, spam-word checker) | ✅ | **Partial** (manual seed entry; no API, no blacklist, no content lint) | **high** |
| Sending schedules / timezones / per-inbox windows | ✅ | **Partial** (one campaign window; per-inbox fields unused; no day-of-week) | med |
| **Template library** | ✅ | **No** | med |
| **Webhooks + public API + API keys** | ✅ | **No** (inbound feedback stub only) | med |
| **Agency sub-accounts / workspaces / white-label portal** | ✅ (Smartlead, EmailBison) | **No** (single admin; Brand≠tenant) | med (Nxeon roadmap) |
| Lead sourcing / enrichment | ✅ (Apollo 210M+) | **No** (manual/CSV) | med (licensing-gated) |
| Multichannel (LinkedIn / SMS / calls) | ✅ (Apollo, Lemlist) | **No** | low for v1 |

Sources: Smartlead master-inbox & subsequences ([smartlead.ai](https://www.smartlead.ai/blog/master-inbox-new-features), [amplemarket audit](https://www.amplemarket.com/blog/what-does-smartlead-really-do)); Instantly unibox/CRM/deliverability/verification ([instantly.ai](https://instantly.ai/blog/instantly-features/)); Apollo sequences+dialer+enrichment & Lemlist liquid/dynamic-image/unified-inbox ([saleshive Apollo](https://saleshive.com/vendors/apollo-io), [heyreach Lemlist](https://www.heyreach.io/blog/lemlist-review)); Woodpecker A/B variants + branching & EmailBison agency workspaces ([syncgtm Woodpecker](https://syncgtm.com/blog/woodpecker-review), [emailbison](https://emailbison.com/blogs/emailbison-vs-woodpecker)).

---

## 3. Overhaul plan — prioritized, phased build spec

Guiding principle: **do NOT rebuild the engine.** The compliance/warmup/rotation/analytics core is
the moat. Build the *product* on top of it — the reply loop, the builder, the pipeline, the polish.
Everything below is additive to the schema (matches the codebase's append-only discipline).

### Phase 1 (of overhaul) — **The Reply Loop + Master Inbox** ← highest impact, mostly buildable now
Turns a blaster into a two-way platform. This is what makes reply-rate (the real 2026 KPI) non-zero.

- **`Inbox` gets real credentials** (schema): `smtpHost/smtpPort/smtpUser/smtpPassEnc/smtpSecure`,
  `imapHost/imapPort/imapUser/imapPassEnc`, `lastImapUid`, `lastPolledAt`. Encrypt with the existing
  `crypto-box`. Makes rotation *real* (each inbox its own mailbox) and unlocks IMAP.
- **IMAP poller** (`worker/coldemail-inbox.ts` + `lib/coldemail/imap.ts`): per-ACTIVE-inbox poll,
  match `In-Reply-To`/`References`/threading + recipient back to a `ColdSend`, write a `REPLY`
  `DeliverabilityEvent` **and an `EmailEvent`**, and — critically — **auto-halt remaining queued
  sends for that contact** (mail-side reply detection, the thing follow-up logic hinges on).
- **New models:** `Conversation` (contactId, campaignId, inboxId, subject, status, lastMessageAt,
  category, assignee) and `Message` (conversationId, direction in/out, fromInbox, raw, snippet,
  sentAt). Threading store for the unibox.
- **Master Inbox UI** (`/admin/coldemail/inbox`): unified list of conversations across all
  campaigns/brands/inboxes, filters (unread / interested / meeting / needs-reply), a thread view,
  and **reply-from-the-right-inbox** compose (reuses `sender.ts` rendering, sends via that inbox's
  SMTP). This is the single most flagship-defining screen.
- **Reply categorization**: rule-based first (OOO / auto-reply / unsubscribe-phrase / bounce
  detection), then an **AI classifier** into Smartlead-style buckets (Interested / Meeting Request /
  Info Request / Not Interested / Do Not Contact / OOO / Wrong Person). Uses the Anthropic API
  already available to the platform — *no new external ESP dependency*.
- **Outbound webhooks** (`Webhook` model + dispatcher): fire on `reply`, `positive_reply`, `bounce`,
  `unsubscribe`, `meeting_booked` so Nxeon/CRMs can subscribe. Cheap, high "platform" signal.
- **Wire real feedback**: connect SES-SNS / Mailcow FBL into `recordFeedback` so bounces/complaints
  arrive live, not by hand.

**Gated on creds:** live *outbound* sending still needs a real sending domain + ESP/Mailcow (the
existing kill-switch). But **IMAP reply capture works the moment one real mailbox exists** — you can
demo the entire inbox/reply/categorize loop on a single test mailbox without flipping the send
switch. New subsystem (not polish): IMAP poller, conversation store, inbox UI, classifier, webhooks.

### Phase 2 — **Visual Sequence Builder + Variants + Spintax/Personalization**
Makes the campaign side feel flagship and directly lifts deliverability (content variation) + reply
rate (personalization).

- **Schema:** `SequenceStep` gains `condition` (ALWAYS / NO_REPLY / NO_OPEN / CLICKED / OPENED),
  `channel` (EMAIL for now), and a child **`StepVariant`** (subject, bodyMarkdown, weight, isControl)
  so A/B variants live under a step; `ColdSend.variantId` for attribution. `Contact` gains a
  **`customFields Json`** bag; `ContactList` import maps arbitrary CSV columns into it.
- **Spintax engine** (`lib/coldemail/spintax.ts`, pure/testable): `{Hi|Hey|Hello}` expansion, seeded
  per-send so it's deterministic + auditable; extend `substitute()` to resolve `{{customField}}` and
  add **fallbacks** (`{{firstName|there}}`). Research §3: sentence-level variation is where the
  deliverability lift is — support paragraph blocks, not just word-level.
- **Visual builder UI** (client component): a vertical step canvas with delay chips, condition
  branches, per-step variant tabs with live reply/positive-reply per variant, and a
  **personalization preview** against a sample contact. Replace the current "Add a step" form.
- **Variant analytics**: extend the rollup to group by `variantId`; auto-surface the winning variant.
- **Template library** (`Template` model + `/admin/coldemail/templates`): save/reuse subject+body
  blocks, seed a starter gallery. Pure UI/CRUD on top of existing rendering.

Mostly pure/UI work — no external creds. New subsystem: spintax + variant engine + builder UI.

### Phase 3 — **CRM / Lead Pipeline + Pre-send Verification + Deliverability Suite**
- **Lead pipeline:** `Contact` (or a new `Lead`) gains `stage` (NEW / CONTACTED / INTERESTED /
  MEETING_BOOKED / WON / LOST / DNC), `ownerId`, `lastActivityAt`; a **kanban board**
  (`/admin/coldemail/pipeline`) mirroring the existing `/admin/agency/pipeline` pattern. Reply
  categorization (Phase 1) auto-advances stages (Interested→INTERESTED, Meeting→MEETING_BOOKED).
- **Pre-send email verification** (`lib/coldemail/verify.ts` + provider seam): syntax/MX/disposable
  checks locally now; ZeroBounce/Bouncer/NeverBounce adapter behind an interface (creds-gated).
  Block/flag a campaign whose projected bounce (from verification sample) exceeds ~3% (research §3).
  Populate the existing but unused `Contact.emailStatus`.
- **Deliverability suite** completion: **blacklist monitor** (query Spamhaus/Barracuda DNSBLs for
  sending IPs/domains via the same authoritative-resolver pattern in `dns.ts` — buildable now, no
  creds), **spam-word / content linter** on step bodies pre-send, and a **placement-test API adapter**
  (GlockApps/MailReach) writing the same `PlacementTest` rows the manual form already does.
- **Richer analytics**: per-campaign time-series charts, step + variant funnels, per-inbox/domain
  health trend lines. Presentation upgrade over the solid existing math.

Verification + placement APIs are creds-gated; blacklist monitor + content lint + charts are not.

### Phase 4 — **Agency workspaces + API + scale polish** (aligns with Nxeon ventures/agency roadmap)
- **`Workspace`/tenant** model wrapping brands/domains/inboxes/campaigns; RBAC scoping; a
  white-label **client portal** (read-only dashboards) — matches EmailBison/Smartlead agency mode and
  the multi-brand goal in `architecture.md`.
- **Public REST API + `ApiKey`** model (create leads, launch campaigns, read stats) — turns it into a
  platform Nxeon's other ventures can drive.
- **Lead sourcing/enrichment** (Apollo/PDL/Hunter behind the licensing guardrails already documented
  in `architecture.md` §3) — the only piece with real ToS/legal gating.

### What's genuinely gated on external creds (call it out to the owner)
1. **Live outbound sending** — a real dedicated sending domain + ESP (SES) or Mailcow inboxes, then
   flip `cold_email_sending_enabled`. Everything else can be built and demoed without it.
2. **Per-inbox IMAP/SMTP creds** — needed for real rotation + reply capture. *One* test mailbox is
   enough to demo the whole reply loop.
3. **Email-verification provider** (ZeroBounce/Bouncer) and **placement-test provider**
   (GlockApps/MailReach) — API keys; local heuristics + manual seed entry work meanwhile.
4. **Enrichment provider** (Apollo/PDL) — licensing + ToS review (Phase 4).

### Pure UI/UX polish vs new subsystems (quick tag)
- **New subsystems:** IMAP poller + conversation store + master inbox (P1), reply classifier +
  webhooks (P1), spintax/variant engine (P2), verification + blacklist monitor (P3), workspaces +
  public API (P4).
- **UI/UX polish (no/low backend):** visual sequence builder, template gallery, pipeline kanban,
  time-series/variant charts, warming activity feed honesty, unified nav shell.

---

## 4. The single biggest thing

**Build the unified Master Inbox with live IMAP reply capture (Phase 1).**

It is the one change that flips the product's whole identity. Today the engine is *deaf* — it sends
sequences but has zero visibility into answers, so its own hero metric (reply / positive-reply rate)
is structurally always zero, follow-up-stops-on-reply can't work, and there is nothing for an
operator to *do* between campaign launches. Every flagship (Instantly Unibox, Smartlead Master Inbox,
Lemlist unified inbox) leads with exactly this screen because it is where outreach becomes a
conversation and a booked meeting. It also uniquely leverages what's already strong here — the
tracking/suppression/threading spine and the Anthropic API for categorization/drafting — and it is
**demoable on a single real mailbox without ever enabling bulk sending**, sidestepping the deploy
gate. Ship the reply loop and the platform stops feeling like a send tool and starts feeling like
Smartlead.

## Summary

**Verdict:** The compliance/deliverability engine (suppression, RFC-8058 unsubscribe, reputation isolation, complaint circuit-breaker, warmup ramp, health auto-pause, DNS auth verify, MPP-honest analytics) is genuinely flagship-grade — arguably better-architected than competitors. But the product is **send-only**: it never reads a reply, never scores a lead, and gives the operator forms instead of a workspace. That's why it feels barebones.

**Top 5 gaps:**
1. **No reply ingestion / master inbox** — `REPLY` events roll up but nothing writes them; no IMAP poller, no conversation store, no unibox. Every flagship's headline feature ([Smartlead](https://www.smartlead.ai/blog/master-inbox-new-features), [Instantly](https://instantly.ai/blog/instantly-features/), [Lemlist](https://www.heyreach.io/blog/lemlist-review)) is 0% built.
2. **No visual sequence builder / conditions / A/B variants** — linear steps only; competitors branch on opens/replies with ≤5 variants ([Woodpecker](https://syncgtm.com/blog/woodpecker-review)).
3. **No CRM/lead pipeline** — Contact has no stage/owner; Instantly & Smartlead ship built-in CRMs.
4. **No pre-send email verification** — post-send bounce control only.
5. **Thin personalization** — 5 hardcoded `{{vars}}`, no spintax, no custom fields (vs [Lemlist liquid/dynamic](https://www.heyreach.io/blog/lemlist-review)). Also: inboxes have no SMTP/IMAP creds, so "rotation" is From-header rotation over one relay.

**Recommended Phase 1 (highest-impact slice): the Reply Loop + Master Inbox.** Add real IMAP creds to `Inbox`, an IMAP poller that matches replies to sends (auto-halting follow-ups), a `Conversation`/`Message` store, a unified inbox UI with reply-from-correct-inbox compose, AI reply categorization (via the platform's existing Anthropic API — no new ESP), and outbound webhooks. It makes reply-rate non-zero, needs no bulk-send switch, and is **demoable on a single test mailbox**. This one screen flips the product's identity from blaster to platform.
